name: China economy
summary: China's new bank loans shrank by about 100bn yuan in October and loan growth hit a record low; no deflation or contagion
state: China's new yuan loans contracted by about 100 billion yuan in October against forecasts of a small rise, with household loans down 430 billion yuan and outstanding loan growth at a record low of 4.7% (The Standard, citing central bank data). Consumer prices rose 0.7% in the year to October, so deflation is not present. Weak credit demand reflects the prolonged property downturn, but no new developer default wave or financial contagion was found as of 13 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: Weak borrowing by Chinese households and firms tends to soften demand for imports and commodities. Exporters to China and companies reliant on Chinese consumers are most exposed; a deeper credit slowdown would raise the risk of property-sector stress spreading.
rubric_hit: Normal: CPI +0.7% (no deflation); no renewed developer defaults or contagion found; weak credit noted

sources.title: The Standard — China's October new bank loans shrink for third time this year as credit demand weakens

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
